title: Money, Honesty, and Hard Lessons
overview: A loose collection of short sayings about honesty, money and friendship, anger, family life, laziness, and the limits of human plans.

parts.label: Honesty and blame (vv. 1-3, 5, 9, 28)
parts.note: Being poor and honest beats being a fool who lies, and people who wreck their lives through rash choices often rage at the LORD instead of themselves. Verses 5 and 9, nearly identical, and verse 28 warn that a false witness, someone who lies in court, mocks justice and will not escape punishment.

parts.label: Money and fair-weather friends (vv. 4-7)
parts.note: Rich and generous people draw crowds of friends, while the poor are avoided even by relatives, who disappear when asked for help. These lines describe how people behave rather than approve of it, and the last line of verse 7 is hard to read in the original Hebrew.

parts.label: Anger, patience and kings (vv. 11-12, 19)
parts.note: Wisdom makes a person slow to anger, and letting an offense go is a mark of honor, while a hot-tempered person keeps needing to be rescued. A king's anger is as frightening as a lion's roar, but his favor is as welcome as dew, which kept plants alive in a dry land.

parts.label: Homes, parents and children (vv. 13-14, 18, 26)
parts.note: Written from a father's point of view, these lines compare a quarrelsome wife to a roof that never stops dripping, call a sensible wife a gift from the LORD, and condemn a child who robs a father and drives out a mother. Verse 18 urges correcting children while there is still hope, but its second line is unclear: it may warn that neglect leads to ruin, or that punishing in a rage can do deadly harm.

parts.label: Laziness and learning (vv. 15, 20, 24-25)
parts.note: The lazy man in verse 24 has his hand in the shared dinner bowl but is too idle to lift it back to his mouth, a deliberately comic picture. Taking advice makes a person wise over time, and when a mocker is punished, naive onlookers learn caution, while rebuking a sensible person adds to their knowledge.

parts.label: Kindness and God's purposes (vv. 17, 21-23)
parts.note: Being kind to the poor is pictured as lending to the LORD, who will pay the loan back. People make many plans, but the LORD's purpose is what stands, and the "fear of the LORD," meaning deep respect for God, is said to lead to a settled, secure life.

think: When something goes wrong in your life, how do you tell what came from your own choices and what was simply out of your hands?
